Having seen and worshipped her, a man prospers in happiness;
because Hara [Śiva] was at the feet of the Goddess, she is therefore remembered as Pādaharā. ||15||
Having bathed there and seen her, one should thereafter behold Maheśvara— she who is the goddess Pādaharā, the bestower of happiness upon men.
In the second interpretation, she who bestows welfare upon all is found by bathing at the Vindūdbhava tīrtha and beholding the auspicious Pādaharā. (17)
Therefore, by worshipping Tīrtheśvara, a man is liberated from sin; likewise, by bathing at Vindutīrtha and beholding Śrī Puruṣottama, a man is liberated. (18)
Having seen the goddess Pādaharā, one indeed obtains imperishable fruit; and he who beholds that liṅga named Tribhuvaneśvara [attains the same]. ||19||
The God of gods, the Lord of the universe, bestows liberation upon him who has bathed in that most excellent of holy places and beheld Śrīdhara-Śaṅkara. ||20||
By means of a celestial chariot that moves at will, one shall attain the supreme station of Viṣṇu;
and Vindūdbhava is declared to be the most excellent of all sacred fords (tīrthas). ||21||
O Brahmins, this auspicious sacred site Vindūdbhava has been described;
I shall now speak of another—what, O Brahmins, do you say is auspicious? ||22||
Whoever reads or hears this narrative of merit, having brought about the destruction of all sins, shall attain immortality. ||23||
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Origin of Vindu," in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||12||
Now begins the thirteenth chapter.
The sages said:
"Relate in detail the supreme majesty of this sacred field."
The majesty of Vāsudeva and that of Koṭiliṅgeśvara. ||1||
Bharadvāja said:
"The glorious forest of Ekāmraka is the most excellent among sacred fields;
O best of the twice-born, there is no field on earth equal to Ekāmraka. (2)
That alone is the supreme abode, that alone is the supreme state;
there all the gods, together with Vāsava, dwell free from fear. ||3||
For this place known as Ekāmravana consists of all sacred fords; in this very ford, the Supreme Brahman dwells in person in the form of a liṅga. ||4||
Ekāmraka is of great merit, its fruit surpassing that of all other sacred fields; it bestows both worldly desires and liberation, and increases all forms of virtue. ||5||
Those men who go there with their minds firmly resolved quickly burn away their sins and indeed uplift their entire lineages.
I do not see any field at all equal to Ekāmra, where even sinners, having gone there, may obtain supreme liberation. (7)
Those best of men who cast off their bodies in that forest go into the presence of Śiva, shining with splendor and speaking kindly. ||8||
Even one burdened by ten million killings, a killer of cows, or a violator of the Guru’s bed—
upon seeing the form of the Single Mango tree, they go to the eternal Viṣṇu.
O twice-born ones, even a worm that casts off its body in the water between Hari and Śaṅkara, born from a drop [of their union], surely attains the supreme state. ||10||
O best of the twice-born, he who casts off his body in the water before the presence of Śrī Vāsudeva merges into Vāsudeva. (11)
There, having cast off their own bodies, even insects and other such crawling creatures as well as all others proceed upon the path of liberation; what then to speak of human beings? ||12||
When a living being abandons its own body at Ekāmra,
the venerable Lord Śambhu, the Giver, shall recite this into the root of its ear.
You shall cast off this body here; go to the supreme, eternal Vaiṣṇava realm, Oṃkāra, which was attained by you through your previously performed merit. 14.
Having thus recited this mantra at the root of his ear and dispatched his own attendants, Maheśvara will certainly lead him to Nirvāṇa.
O twice-born ones, to the south of the king of elephants stands the Āmalaka tree;
it removes all sins and was created by the Lord himself. ||16||
O Brahmins, this tree certainly always performs auspicious deeds dear to Vāsudeva, because it stands upon the king of sacred fields; such is its distinction. (17)
O Brahmins, even those who were the worst of sinners attained liberation by casting off their bodies at its root; how much more so, then, for those of meritorious deeds? (18)
And for those who had committed acts of distrust, the Supreme Lord made this Ālaka tree a means for their restoration of faith. ||19||
There, having cast off the body anywhere—in a single mango grove, outdoors, in the air, in water, or on land—one shall attain liberation. ||20||
O best of the twice-born, whether one is of evil conduct or of virtuous conduct, if that person leaves the single mango tree and your body, he shall attain Vaikuṇṭha.
Such are the various qualities of that single mango grove, where the Lord of the World himself is present and is considered to grant liberation through the mere sight of him. (22)
He who beholds Vighneśvara, the bull, the god [Śiva], the goddess [Pārvatī], the illustrious Guha, the tree [Aśvattha], and Sāvitrī, shall never again be one who drinks from his mother’s breast.
The birth of those fortunate ones who worship Koṭiliṅgeśvara there with a concentrated mind is proclaimed to be fruitful. ||24||
With perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and even food offerings, as well as with garlands and betel, [one worships] Śiva in the grove of Ekāmra. (25)
O best of the twice-born, listen as I describe the destiny of those foremost among men who worship with hearts full of fervent devotion. ||26||
With various kinds of celestial palaces frequented by *siddhas* and *gandharvas*, with auspicious banners and flags, and with dances performed by hosts of *apsarases*. ||27||
O Indra, they were fashioned from materials resembling sapphire and like ruby, encased in gold and pearls, and adorned with the feathers of peacocks and *śaṅkara* birds. ||28||
Those men whose minds have seen [the Lord] attain proximity to Śiva;
there, those human beings enjoy all desired pleasures. ||29||
This god Rūpākṣa is undoubtedly of the nature of Brahman;
by the mere sight of him, the sin of killing a Brahmin is destroyed. ||30||
Those who constantly behold with devotion the Imperishable One in the form of a Liṅga in the Ekāmravana forest, for them liberation is held in the palm of their hand. ||31||
O best of Brahmins, the food offering (naivedya) of whichever deity destroys great sins is to be enjoyed by the gods, beginning with Brahmā.
O Brahmins, in the forest of Ekāmra is the eternal Liṅga in person,
for which offerings of food are desired by Śakra and the other dwellers of heaven.
"O twice-born ones, those statements which say that the offering to the Lord (īśa-naivedya) is ungraspable and should not be consumed—never are they respected in this matter. (34)
The great sages have declared that the food offering (naivedya) is the "Great Grace" (mahāprasāda), O best of Brahmins, within the body of Viṣṇu in the forest of Ekāmra. (35)
Do not set a limit on the number of food offerings made to the holy Liṅgarāja;
by disregarding this, people go to hell—of this there is no doubt. (36)

That excellent man who performs the supreme raising of the banner for that Śrī Liṅgarāja attains the state of Śiva; likewise, [he who honors it] with silk cloths, blue garments, and yellow or white raiment. (37)
Those best of men who perform the hoisting of the banner for the Lord there, having destroyed sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, [attain liberation]. ||38||
Having rescued their ancestors from hell, they go certainly to the auspicious state;
and whoever causes the sound of a drum to be heard there at the time of worship, [attains the same]. ||39||
And with the sound of mṛdaṅgas and conchs, as well as paṭahas, bherīs, kāhalas, and ṛṇibhas, O best of men, they [proceeded] according to the ancient tradition. (40)
Enveloped by those sounds, they proceed to the immutable Śiva;
O twice-born ones, upon merely hearing that sound, a man shall attain liberation.

Beholding his worship, I know not what fruit might accrue; he who here in this world recites the mantra with devotion before Koṭiliṅgeśvara shall be happy and enjoy worldly pleasures, and at the end of the body, attain Śiva. ||42||
That which is Koṭiliṅgeśvara is indeed Brahman itself, there is no doubt;
beholding it, men constantly attain their heart's desire. ||43||
All the deities, beginning with Brahmā, worship him day and night with devotion at this sacred site born from the Bindu, and thereby attain their own respective abodes. ||44||
There is no linga equal to the Koṭiliṅgeśvara;
on earth, in Bhogavatī, or in heaven—truly, truly I tell you this.
O Brahmins, by the mere sight of him who is the Lord of the three worlds in the Ekāmra forest, a person attains liberation. ||46||
For those who perform circumambulation of Koṭiliṅgeśvara step by step, the state of Brahman shall be near at hand.
Having approached Caṇḍeśvara, one who performs circumambulation by leaping over the Soma-sūtra from left to right or right to left incurs hell. ||48||
O twice-born ones, having seen and worshipped Him there before the king of bulls in His own embodied form, a person shall obtain the grace of Śiva. (49)
Having worshipped Sāvitrī, who is situated in the southwestern direction at the rear of the God, and having beheld her, one shall obtain one's desire. ||50||
Having first beheld Vighneśvara, and having diligently worshipped Caṇḍī and the daughter of Himādri at his side, he seeks to destroy the hells. ||51||
Having beheld Śikhidhvaja situated slightly to the north on the northern side of the deity, a man shall obtain prosperity. ||52||
To the east of that [place], there is one known as Ekāmreśvara;
in a former kalpa, an *ekāmravṛkṣa* tree stood there, which bestows liberation. (53)
There, one mango tree had gone [there], and from that came the forest of Ekāmraka—a tree of great height, with beautiful branches and most enchanting foliage. (54)
The destroyer of the Asuras made that tree—the source of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, as well as leaves, wood, and fruit—worthy of being protected. ||55||
Its root is Śameśa, by whose name it has become renowned;
having seen him with the prescribed mantra, one shall attain virtue, desire, and wealth. (56)
There, on the peak of Śrīśaila, stands a great tree called Tiktaśāka; in ancient times, the Blessed Lord Śambhu planted that tree.
Listen to the greatness of that tree, which destroys sins,
as it occurred in the past during the great and extremely perilous battle between the gods and the asuras.
All the heavens were conquered by the Rākṣasas, who were arrogant in their strength;
then Indra, filled with apprehension, spoke these words to Bṛhaspati.
Bṛhaspati said:
"Go to Ekāmra, O Lord of Śacī; behold the eternal God there.
Having performed austerities upon the surface of the bitter-leafed tree (tiktaśāka), you shall be victorious."
Having heard these words of his, he who was intent on the destruction of the wicked chanted for a long time that supreme mantra of splendor.
Then the illustrious Lord Bharga, gratified by his ascetic penance, spoke these beautiful, well-composed, and appropriate words to the slayer of Bala:
Śaṅkara said:
"O Pākaśāsana, listen; I am this tree manifest before you.
By chanting a mantra at its root, I shall grant you your desired boon. (63)
Now let it be offered as a sacrifice; in that forest of Ekāmra, you shall be the conqueror of the Daityas—engage in battle in that forest of Ekāmra! (64)
Then the Lord of the Thirty-three, having accepted the destruction of the sacrifice, departed for heaven accompanied by all the deities.
Then, by the command of the God of gods, the slayer of Bala waged war with the Daityas and struck down the boon-granting Dānavas.
Then a shower of flowers fell from the sky upon the head of Puruhūta,
and all the deities departed for their respective cities.
In this way, the Śrītiktaśāka tree is the bestower of supreme accomplishment;
by beholding it while reciting its own mantra, one shall attain the fulfillment of one's heart's desire.
Thus have I related to you in brief the exceedingly pure majesty of this tree;
having performed supreme austerity at its root in former times, O twice-born ones, the lord of the gods slew the Daityas. (69)
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Enhancement of Indra’s Yoga," in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||13||
Now begins the fourteenth chapter.
Bharadvāja said:
"O twice-born ones, I shall now declare the majesty of Vāsudeva."
By chanting the praises of Vāsudeva, a person shall attain liberation. ||1||
There, in the holy Ekāmra, Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world, having abandoned Vaikuṇṭha, dwells in personified form himself. ||2||
His arms were adorned with bracelets well-fashioned from various jewels; his waist was decorated with tinkling bells, and his feet were like fresh sprouts. ||3||
With eyes rolling in sleep from the *jambū*, *nīpa*, *kadamba*, and other flowers, he shone upon his cheeks with two wonderful earrings. ||4||
Resplendent with matted locks and with knitted brows, possessing the brilliance of the sky, dark as a sapphire, his body marked with the Śrīvatsa. ||5||
His lower lip, resembling a pomegranate flower, bestows nectar;
he stands in the form of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, the bearer of Lakṣmī. ||6||
This very one, whose nature is manifest Brahman, is declared to be the Supreme Brahman—non-dual, imperishable, eternal, and known by the name Vāsudeva. ||7||
He alone is the giver of the [various] destinies, and He alone is the Supreme Self;
He dwells within the heart, even among worms, trees, and moths. ||8||
Or those who speak ill of Vāsudeva, the stainless one who pervades all, do not see him through devotion; they are cooked for a long time in the Raurava hell. (9)
Having abandoned all delightful fields, sacred fords, and shrines, O Lord of the World, You have taken Your abode in the Ekāmra forest. ||10||
O Brahmins, Ekāmra does not meet with destruction even at the time of universal dissolution;
therefore, Gadādhara remains there, having abandoned all else. ||11||
Ekāmraka and Vindusarovara are the supreme beyond the supreme, the eternal self that is Brahman;
they are the Lord who is without a superior, the eternal Ishvara, Hari, dark-hued and radiant as the sun. 12.

Having realized that the reality of Yama is of the nature of Brahman—the beloved of devotees, tranquil, stainless, and possessing a sublime form—one who examines the mind and its measurements attains whatever fruit is described as belonging to the lake. ||13||
That Murāri, the remover of the suffering of the world, shines alone for the sake of protection;
he bears the Kaumodakī mace, the conch, and the discus, wears yellow garments, and wears the Kaustubha gem. ||14||

He whose nature is Brahman, who has subdued all impurity, who is dear to his devotees, whose blemishes are stilled, and who possesses a sublime body—having understood the fruit of the lake of the Rākṣasas of the mind and ego, he bestows it exactly as described. ||15||
By the sight of Śrī Vāsudeva, Dakṣa, Śeṣa, and Gadāyudha, those who were deceitful, wicked, and engaged in atheistic deeds attained liberation at Ekāmra. 16.
That all-pervading Lord, Murāri, the slayer of Madhu—
the Blessed One himself— resides in the midst of the Ekāmravana forest.
Having abandoned all the sacred fords on earth and the hermitages of the sages, Hari himself assumed the form of a stone.
On the Blue Mountain (Nīlādri), Hari might at some time abandon his wooden body; but at Ekāmra, he never abandons it, for he ever shines there with his stone-blue form.
Lord Hari, the bearer of the conch and discus, dwells in the midst of the Ekāmravana forest;
by the mere remembrance of him, all sins go to their destruction. (20)
I do not know what fruit there is in beholding that deity;
however, by meditating upon and worshipping Puruṣottama, a man will surely attain liberation in the Ekāmravana forest. ||21||
"I shall go to Ekāmraka; I shall behold Puruṣottama"—he whose mouth utters these words shall also go to the city of Viṣṇu. (22)
Likewise, having abandoned all other holy places, Ekamra is Puruṣottama;
for that which is always chanted as the *praṇava* in the Veda and the Purāṇas is that very *praṇava* who eternally shines there, bearing a body of stone. (23)
That which is the supreme Brahman in the world of Brahmā, the Grandfather, and that which is Brahman in the four Vedas and the Śāstras— that is this very Śilāṅgaka.
Having bathed there at Vindūdbhava and beholding the lotus-face [of the deity], one becomes fulfilled even while living; of this there is no doubt. ||25||
Beholding the lotus-face of that Lord in the form of Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, as well as Śuka and the others, attained supreme liberation. ||26||
To those best of men who sing "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" before Him, He—the friend of His devotees—bestows liberation through His grace. ||27||
But that man who drinks the water arising from his feet—his external and internal sin is destroyed; it is not otherwise. ||28||
Whatever mortal performs a prostration like a staff before that Janārdana, his merit shall truly be equal to that arising from a hundred horse-sacrifices. (29)
And by the circumambulation of that Śrī Vāsudeva performed even as a mere playfulness, thousands of sins of Brahman-slaughter are destroyed at every step. ||30||
O Brahmins, in the forest of Ekāmra, Janārdana, the God of gods, is that very Supreme Brahman who bestows supreme bliss. (31)
At Ekāmra, the Supreme Brahman known as Vāsudeva—bestower of liberation and destroyer of demons—grants devotion even through a stone form. ||32||
Reciting that mantra before him while meditating upon Puruṣottama, that man who is devoted to Viṣṇu goes to Vaikuṇṭha. ||33||
O best of sages, whether one has performed a righteous deed or an unrighteous one, a person attains Vaikuṇṭha simply by beholding that Janārdana; it is not otherwise.
O twice-born ones, you should indeed know Vaikuṇṭha to be the abode of Vāsudeva;
whoever always dwells there shall become liberated while yet living (jīvanmukta). ||35||
Thus, there are manifold virtues belonging to Vāsudeva, the wielder of the discus, by the mere remembrance of whom even the sin of killing a Brahmin and other such offenses pass away. ||36||

Worship Hari, whose arms are marked with the conch and the discus, who dwells alone in the forest of mango trees, whose eyes are like lotuses, who wears yellow garments, and who has the luster of a rain cloud. 37.
O twice-born ones, Vāsudeva truly bestows liberation upon that person who recites this mantra with a spirit endowed with devotion. (38)
And at the end of a thousand yojanas, he who worships the mantra "śaṅkhacakra" shall attain rare liberation and depart as a bearer of the conch. ||39||
O best of the twice-born, there is no formal initiation required for this mantra; it should be recited by every living being, for it grants liberation and leads one to Hari. (40)
It must not be given to one who is cruel or devoid of devotion; it should be kept secret, and it must never be spoken of to another person. ||41||
O Brahmins, this mantra of the conch and discus is remembered by the wise as the king of mantras; it is a supreme, secret mantra that must be kept hidden, which has been told to you by me.
O Brahmins, in that Puṇyavana forest, the Liṅga known as Brahmeśvara is remembered;
by the mere sight of it, one shall attain the world of Brahmā. ||43||
Bhāskareśa, Megheśa, the one known as Gokarṇeśvara, the Svarṇajāleśvara Liṅga, and likewise Svarṇakūṭeśvara; ||44||
Having seen these, having paid homage, and having worshipped them with diligence, one abandons all evil and goes to the abode of Kailāsa. ||45||
O twice-born ones, by worshipping and beholding that Sūkṣmeśvara Liṅga of the God of gods, Āgneya, one shall cast off a heap of sins. (46)
Right there are Āmrātakeśa and Madhyameśvara; by the sight of these two, O brahmins, one obtains the fruit of residing in Kāśī. ||47||
Offering a ball of rice (piṇḍa) right there to the ancestors on the subtle southern side, a man, having delivered his ancestors from hell, shall go to the world of the gods. ||48||
Whoever offers a funeral rice-ball (piṇḍa) at that site of Sūkṣmeśvara, bowing his head, provides inexhaustible satisfaction for the ancestors. 49.
O twice-born ones, I shall describe the specific details regarding the place and time:
on the new moon day of the month of Āśvina, one who is self-controlled, restrained, and pure [should perform it]. (50)
Whoever performs the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍas) to the south of Śrīsūkṣmeśvara, his ancestors remain satisfied for the duration of hundreds of millions of kalpas. ||51||
In its western direction, the god known as Kapileśvara,
who grants all desires, was worshipped by Kapila.
The auspicious Linga Kapileśa bestows the desires of the gods and grants the fruits of the heart's wishes for all living beings. ||53||
Therein lies the Śrīkāpila pool, which bestows the fruit of all holy fords;
having bathed there and beheld the forest, one shall indeed attain imperishable merit. ||54||
There, situated in the northern direction, is the Ugreśvara Liṅga;
he alone is the lord of ten million and one hundred thousand Liṅgas.
Having seen that [liṅga], one endowed with joy shall obtain eleven lakhs [of merits];
there, Nandīśvara himself is present before the God, as well as Bhṛkuṭī.
Having seen and paid homage to those two, a human being attains happiness;
there resides Yameśvara, situated in the direction of the Wind-god (the northwest). ||57||
O Brahmins, the staff of Yama does not afflict that man who beholds it;
before him lies the supreme holy site known as Pāpanāśana (the Destroyer of Sins). ||58||
O best of the twice-born, sins go to destruction merely by bathing in its waters on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.
Having bathed there and offered libations to the ancestors, whoever beholds Yama and Varuṇa—for him Śambhu shall be pleased, especially in the Kali age. (60)
There, that best of men who duly performs the rite at the eight sacred fords shall reach the world of Śiva and never leave it.
On the southern side of the Kuṇḍa is the one known as Īśāneśvara; by resorting to him according to the prescribed rites, one shall attain the station of Indra.
The sacred Ekāmrakānana is filled with ten million liṅgas and endowed with ten million holy bathing-places (tīrthas); it increases the victory of the gods. ||63||
And there are many lingas there, O best of the twice-born; Śeṣa himself would not be able to state the number of those Śiva-lingas.
Who is able to describe the virtues of the single mango grove and its delightful hermitages, where great sages dwell? (65)
O Brahmins, I have here spoken something most excellent to you; O ascetics, what else do you wish to hear with faith? ||66||
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "Description of Various Liṅgas," in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa concerning Ekāmraka. ||14||
Now begins the fifteenth chapter.
The sages said:
O best of sages, what further supreme stage of life (āśrama) exists?
Speak everything in its entirety within that single Aśoka grove.
Bharadvāja said: O brahmins, in that sacred forest, to the north of the God of gods, there is the one renowned as Rāmeśvara, which was worshipped by Rāmacandra. ||2||
That auspicious place, which bestows merit, was the hermitage of Rāmacandra;
it was crowded with various hosts of sages and honored by Brahmā and Vāsava. ||3||
It was adorned with bakula, panasa, and mango trees, and filled on all sides with many birds and many deer. ||4||
That great place of Raghunātha increases one's spiritual merit through austerity; there dwells the Lord of Jānakī, who eternally worships that Śiva. ||5||
There, to the west of that Liṅga, is the famous Tīrtha known as Aśokavāra, which arose from the sacrifice and destroys all sins.
O Brahmins, there is no sacred site on this earth superior to Aśoka, where a man, having bathed, goes to the world of Śiva.
He who bathes there with fervor, having meditated upon Maheśvara in his heart—especially on the eighth day of the bright fortnight—is not immersed in sins. ||8||
O best of sages, in the northern direction there is the famous and beautiful hermitage of Uttareśvara, which destroys all sins along with the Sasośca mountain.
Having restrained his mind, he indeed recited it before the Goddess and likewise before the Lord; it was beautiful, completed in three fortnights, and filled by the best of sages.
It was filled with Aśoka, Nīpa, Lodhra, Vakula, and Nāgakeśara trees,
joined by Mālatī and Mādhavī vines, and endowed with excellent fragrances.
In the same way, it was adorned with mangoes and emblic myrobalans bearing fruit, as well as with oleanders, karnikaras, trumpet-flowers, and mango trees. ||12||
Thus filled with various kinds of trees, it is exceedingly beautiful;
there stands the Siddheśvara Liṅga, which bestows liberation.
In the center, it takes the form of a lotus pond, beautifully adorned with blue water-lilies; its waters are divine, ever-meritorious, cool, and free from mud. ||14||
Having fully propitiated Siddheśvara, the sages of supreme austerity attained the highest perfection both in this world and in the next. ||15||
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a god superior to Siddheśvara;
having seen him, one is liberated from sin, and for such a man, there is no longer the state of being a slayer of a Brahmin.
He who offers salutation with his body bowed down by the head—he indeed is the Lord Viṣṇu; he indeed is the Lord Śiva. ||17||
The Blessed Lord Śiva, who is perfected throughout the fourteen worlds, attains oneness with Śiva; therefore, he is remembered as Siddheśvara. ||18||
Upon seeing it, one is liberated from sin; by touching it, one attains long life;
through worship, one attains liberation—this truth, this truth, I have spoken.
On its right side is a pool that destroys sins, renowned by his name; having bathed there, the water becomes perfectly pure. (20)
Having bathed there even once, a person rejoices in the vault of heaven; and whoever recites the supreme mantra before Siddheśvara there, [attains success]. ||21||
That mantra bestows success upon him; there is no doubt about this in brief.
Therein lies the Mukteśvara Liṅga, which grants liberation and destroys sins. ||22||
Upon seeing him in the vicinity of that *liṅga*, a man is liberated;
thus, O best of sages, has this supreme sacred field been described by me. (23)
Kapila said:
O King, having heard these words of Bharadvāja,
all the sages were filled with joy and questioned him again with great respect.
We have all achieved our purpose; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt. Yet, a further question has arisen for us regarding the ultimate nature of the field. (25)
O best of Brahmins, if you have compassion for us, please tell us about those liṅgas that are indeed situated near Siddheśvara. (26)
Listen, O tigers among sages, to the auspicious Liṅga Śiśreśvara;
in former times, Viḍaujas, the lord of Śacī, worshipped it.
Having heard these words of those sages of purified souls, the high-minded Bharadvāja spoke these pleasing words: ||28||
Bharadvāja said:
Next, to the east of Siddheśvara, the bestower of all perfections, the god Indreśvara is remembered as being located in that direction. (29)
O twice-born ones, there Indra, surrounded by all the gods, performed a sacrifice; but when that sacrifice had been commenced by Viḍaujas, the sons of Diti created obstacles.
He waged a great battle with the sons of Diti, who were endowed with great strength;
subsequently, Śakra, being defeated, went for refuge to the gods.
Looking toward Śaṅkara, he said: "Save me, O Supreme Lord!
I have indeed been defeated by the Daityas at the time of sacrifice, O Bestower of Victory. (32)
Then, having heard those words, Mahādeva spoke:
"O Lord of Śacī, for your sake indeed I shall subdue the Dānavas."
Having spoken thus, Dhūrjaṭi approached with great speed and,
together with Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendor, struck down all the Dānavas.
Having granted the boon to Maghavan, he then vanished on that very spot;
thereafter, Vṛddhaśravas worshipped Śaṅkara at the Liṅga.
Having duly worshipped the Liṅga with fragrant sandalwood and enchanting incense and lamps, he departed for Amaravatī.
Thus, O sinless ones, the origin of Indreśvara has been made known from of old;
by the greatness of Indreśvara, all impurities go to their destruction. (37)
This is considered the sovereign abode of Indra, bestowing all merit;
it is crowded with various sages and resplendent with every kind of tree. ||38||
Those best of men who, as devotees, worship that Lord, go after death to the supreme abode which is difficult even for the gods to attain. (39)
Those men who worship that Lord even with blades of durvā grass go to the stainless abode, shining with great splendor. ||40||
Thus, O best of sages, the narrative of Indra known as the "Lord" has been told;
it removes all sins, is meritorious, supreme, and a great means of securing well-being. 41.
O twice-born ones, he who hears this work of the sages but does not honor the reciter, his eyes and ears shall become deaf.
Therefore, one should worship him with fruits, garments, and gold; in this way, Indraśvara will surely be gracious toward his devotees. ||43||
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Narrative of Indreśvara," in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||15||
Now begins the sixteenth chapter.
Bharadvāja said:
Having paid homage to Maheśvara, I shall now describe that which is of great merit.
To the south of Siddhinātha is the one known as Kedāreśvara. ||1||
Having reached the sacred site of Kedāreśa and worshipped Maheśāna with supreme devotion, a person shall obtain their desired fruit. ||2||
He is named Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the bestower of all spiritual attainments;
by the mere sight of him, may there be the fruit of the Vājapeya and Aśvamedha sacrifices. ||3||
And whoever always serves the interior of the Liṅga in the west, south, and likewise in the north, purifies the entire earth and the intermediate realm. ||4||
Any man or woman who, being devoted to Śiva, sprinkles their head with [this water], quickly destroys all evil through the grace of Kedāreśa. ||5||

Having ascended them, O Brahmins, those sages then went to the abode of Brahmā together with all their lineages, numbering one thousand seven hundred.
Oh, what great fortune! Oh, what great fortune for the sages who discourse upon Brahman—that a single bath in the Gandhavatī destroys the flood of their sins! (86)
O Brahmins who dwell on Kailāśa, I have heard of your provisions for the journey; this [account] which increases merit has surely been told for your pleasure. (87)
By hearing the majesty of Gandhavatī, one's sin is destroyed;
one attains a long life and the increase of merit.
The man who hears this sacred narrative that increases merit shall never suffer the severance of his wealth or his progeny. (89)
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of Gandhavatī," in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa.
The Eighteenth Chapter. Now I shall describe the Maheśa-tīrtha, which issued from the feet of the illustrious Pārvatī;
having destroyed [her] infamy and established her residence, the Goddess created this sacred ford for the purification of the people. 1.
O best of the twice-born, the pair of feet of the Goddess is a sacred ford at Svarṇakūṭa;
there also lies a lake that is most purifying and honored by all. ||2||
The sages said:
O Brahmin, whose son was Kīrti? Where did he formerly reside?
And who is said to have been his dwelling place? By which goddess were both of them slain? (3)
Who created this excellent holy site fashioned by the foot of the Goddess?
O you of great merit, please tell us this story in detail at once.
O best of sages, I shall relate: there was a great asura named Kīrti, the son of Durbhila, who was wise and the destroyer of aquatic creatures. ||5||
Durmukha, Durjaya, Devakaṇṭaka, Brāhmaṇakaṇṭaka,
and Vāsava— his brothers were intent on the destruction of the entire world.
One hundred and one brothers of his are proclaimed;
all were of terrible strength, formidable, and lived together with those dwelling in the mountains. ||7||
And having abandoned those brothers, Haṃsaka, being constantly threatened by his father under the pretext of hunting deer, went to the Ekāmraka forest.
Having seen her there, the Blessed Lady requested to live together with her; she said, "O noble lady, grant me my life; O beautiful one, protect me! (9)
I am fame and this is my dwelling; there is no one equal to me in the worlds, for I am enriched with sovereignty, virtue, and beauty, and honored for my good fortune and strength. (10)
I am sinking upon seeing you; save me, O lady of excellent complexion!
Protect me, O lotus-eyed one; give me your own body. (11)
Moreover, Yama holds these two feet upon his head; once he is slain, I shall become his eternal beloved—of this there is no doubt. (12)
Having heard these words of hers, the two sons of Durbhila, now empowered and steadfast, were greatly delighted, O daughter of the king of mountains.
Then, with his left foot, he struck the great asura Vāsa, as well as Kīrti and the king of the asuras; and the gods attained great joy.
Then the gods, the inhabitants of heaven, having arrived at the head-abode which destroys sins and possesses a back as pure as crystal, established their station there. ||15||
For the delight of the Goddess, there is a sacred ford that purifies the three worlds, which is honored by many sages and bestows the fruits of the three realms. (16)
Having bathed with devotion at Devīpada on the eighth day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, a person shall obtain their desired wish, equal to that of Gopālana. ||17||
Thus, O best of the twice-born, there are many sacred fords (tīrthas) located there;
what else shall I say regarding that fruit-bestowing field? (18)
O Brahmins, I shall proclaim the purifying names by the mere remembrance of which a man becomes free from sin. (19)
Svarṇakūṭa, Rasāla, Medhya, Ūṣmaśiras, Admas, Laghu, Arjita, Siddhaśaila, Svargastha, and Tapasara-sthalī. (20)
These names are praised as meritorious and destroyers of sin; they should be remembered upon rising in the morning, for they bring happiness to that day. (21)
Kapila said:
O King, having heard these words of Bharadvāja, all those twice-born sages were filled with joy and questioned him once more with great reverence.
The sages said:
O Blessed One, we wish to hear what fruit one might obtain by the Cāturmāsya vow at the temple of Śiva on Svarṇakūṭa.
In this regard, what merit is gained through charity, or what fruit is obtained through austerity?
What merit comes from the gift of food, and which vow should one practice? (24)
Bharadvāja said:
O twice-born ones, I shall describe the highly meritorious ritual of the Cāturmāsya, which, performed in this sacred field in a single day, bestows the fruit of residing in Kāśī. (25)
That man who observes the Cāturmāsya vow in the field of Ekāmraka shall obtain a fruit a hundred times and even more than a thousand times that of Kāśī. ||26||
O twice-born ones, whatever fruit is obtained at Kedāra and whatever fruit is obtained at Puruṣottama, that fruit is multiplied ten millionfold at Svarṇakūṭācala.
The fruit that is proclaimed for Kurukṣetra, for the four months, and during the eclipses of the moon and sun, is said to be obtained at Ekāmra during Cāturmāsya; of this there is no doubt. ||28||
Whatever fruit one might obtain by performing penance at the Godāvarī or the Gaṅgā, that very fruit is obtained in a single day during Cāturmāsya while staying in the abode of Śiva. ||29||
Any person who dwells there, beginning from the very bed, shall obtain a fruit even greater than that of Vārāṇasī and Prayāga. ||30||
Where Viṣṇu is present, surrounded by Vāsava and the other gods—who could possibly describe his majesty and the full extent of his ritual procedures? (31)
But where Kīrtivāsa, the God of gods, resides together with Umā—who indeed would be able to describe his majesty and the full extent of his ritual procedures? (32)
Whatever goal one attains by performing very severe penance for eight yugas at Kāśī, that same goal is attained by staying in a temple of Śiva during Cāturmāsya. ||33||
Whoever should dwell for a single day at Ekāmra after the time of Hari’s sleep,
he indeed attains that goal which belongs to those perfected in Sāṃkhya and Yoga through this vow.
I shall describe the ritual for the Cāturmāsya; listen, O best of sages!
Having reached the tenth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, one should perform the formal resolve (saṃkalpa).
On the ninth day, being well-composed and devoted to Vāsudeva, one should perform the rite of the eight sacred fords (aṣṭatīrtha) and utter this mantra: ||36||
O Madhusūdana, for the destruction of my sins committed since birth, I shall perform the rite of the eight sacred fords; O Janārdana, give me your command. (37)
Having thus taken leave of Govinda, one should then proceed to Vindusaras;
there also, one should utter this request to Vāsudeva.
O Vāsudeva, obeisance to you, O Lord, son of Vasudeva!
O Lord of gods, I wish to bathe; please prepare everything that is required. (39)
Having prayed to Vāsudeva, one should then place the ritual deposit (nyāsa) in the heart; O brahmins, one should place Skanda on the right and Nandikeśvara on the left.
One should place Mahākāla on the left side, the god Ananta on the back, and Vāsudeva upon the head; in this manner, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa). ||41||
Then, having become pure in mind and holding the *pavitra* grass, standing in water reaching to the navel and facing north, one should utter this mantra: ||42||
O Vāsudeva, salutations to you, O Lord, son of Vasudeva; O Lord of gods, I desire to remember [you], so grant me the attainment of perfection. ||43||
O you who arise from a drop, salutations to you; O universal drop fashioned by Mahādeva, O lamp of the world, I immerse myself in your waters. 44.
Having performed the bath by means of this mantra-yoga, the Brahmins, having joined their palms in reverence, should pray with this mantra. ||45||
This is the Lord Viśveśvara; this indeed is Maṇikarṇikā, the portion of Kāśī hidden within, situated right upon his head—of this there is no doubt.
Having bathed in this manner, with his soul purified, and having beheld the three-eyed Lord,
he should proceed to Pāpavināśana in the northwestern direction of the deity.
Then, standing facing the god with palms joined in reverence, he said:
"The presence [of the deity] was previously ordained for you by the wielder of the trident."
"I have attained immeasurable [merit] from you; I shall now plunge into your lake," saying this, he went into the water with a composed mind, facing north. (49)
Having meditated upon Virūpākṣa in the heart, one should then recollect the mantra:
"For he is the sustainer of the world, without beginning or end, bodiless, yet the sustainer of bodies. (50)
Be gracious, O Lord Īśāna; let our devotion here be steadfast.
I shall immerse myself three times while reciting the six-syllabled mantra.
Then, having gone there with diligence, one should behold the Lord of the Three Worlds; furthermore, in the northeastern quarter, there is Gaṅgāyamunamardinī.
Having reached its bank, he should recite the previously mentioned injunction;
then, having gone into the water, facing north and holding the *pavitra* grass, [he should proceed]. (53)
Having recollected the beloved of Candrikā, one should utter this mantra:
"O Bearer of the Gaṅgā, salutations to you at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā. (54)
Having bathed here, which is exceedingly beneficial and consists of the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,
one should indeed bathe with this mantra and then worship Gaṅgā there.
Then, one should diligently behold the Liṅga Tribhuvaneśvara, as well as Koṭitīrtha, which is filled [with merit], belonging to the Lord of the North-Eastern direction. ||56||
Having indeed recalled the prior authorization, one should then utter the mantra:
"I proclaim this entire world as a bath, whatever merit it may possess. (57)
Therefore, O Destroyer of Tripura, may my merit here also be inexhaustible, having bathed there according to the prescribed rite and beheld the Lord of the Three Worlds. (58)
In the eastern direction, one whose self is purified should worship the god Brahmeśvara;
having remembered the previous permission, he should then recollect the mantra. ||59||
Homage be to the Supreme Reality; homage to the Lord of Creatures!
I worship here at the sacrificial pit for the sake of Śambhu, and by your command, I immerse myself. 60.
Then, having beheld the Lord of the Three Worlds, one should proceed to Megheśvara;
recollecting the previous authorization, one should then utter the mantra. ||61||
Salutations to you, O blue-throated one; salutations to the lord of Parjanya!
Be gracious, for you, named Sumukha, shall behold this sacrifice.
Having bathed according to this rite and having beheld that Kapardin, one should proceed to the Ālāmbuka Tīrtha in the northern direction of the God.
Having reached its bank and recalled the previous permission as before, O twice-born ones, he should indeed immerse himself three times with this mantra. (64)
Salutations to you, the eternal one, whose matted hair is the embodiment of meditative yoga;
O Maheśvara, fulfill the attainment of the fruits of my heart's desire! 65.
Then, having gone there and beheld Maheśāna, the Lord of the Three Worlds,
and having saluted and paid homage to him, one should proceed to the Northern Mountain.
One should perform a bath at the place renowned as Rāmeśvara;
having bathed with permission as before, one should utter this mantra: ||67||
On the northern bank of the Vṛṣabha [mountain], you dwell on the southern peak; you are named Aśokavāra—remove my sin, homage be to you! ||68||
Having bathed according to this rite and beheld Śrī Kīrtivāsa, one shall attain the world of light at the conclusion of all sins. ||69||

Having performed the sipping of water at the sacred fords with the eighth verse in this manner, O best of sages, one should observe the practice of eating only once a day or eating only at night on the tenth day. (70)
O best of the twice-born, at night one should sleep on the bare ground after spreading out kuśa grass; and on the tenth day, one should perform the rite of the eight sacred waters (aṣṭatīrtha).
Furthermore, at the time of dawn on the eleventh day, the wise man should perform the ritual bath in Lake Bindusaras and offer salutations to the Lord of Śrī-Ramā.
Having become silent and facing the east, and having meditated upon the Holder of the Śrīcakra within his heart,
he should then request permission from the Lord of the World and perform the formal resolve (saṃkalpa).
O Viṣṇu, act quickly so that my Cāturmāsya vow may be completed without obstacle—this vow which destroys sin and increases merit. (74)
On the eleventh day, with self-restraint, having thus requested permission from Acyuta, one should worship Vighnarāja (Gaṇeśa) with the mantra "gaṇānāṃ tvā". ||75||
Then, having worshipped Vighnarāja alone in the presence of Īśvara and having made a formal resolve according to his desire, that observer of the vow should then perform [the rite].
Thereafter, O brahmins, the observer of the vow should perform his bath every day in that most excellent lake and should behold Śrī Kīrtivāsa daily. (77)
O twice-born ones, a wise Brāhmaṇa, who is clothed in fame, should not make a distinction between the feet of the Goddess and those of Ananta. (78)
The best of those observing the vow should perform their daily viewing of these [deities];
free from envy, he should avoid leafy vegetables during the first month.
O best of the twice-born, one should avoid curd in the month of Bhādrapada, milk in Āśvina, and when the month of Kārttika has arrived, meat should be avoided. 80.
One should indeed offer a lamp daily, dedicated to the head [of the deceased];
he must not look at a woman and should avoid oil and meat. ||81||
When the month of Kārtika has passed, those observing the vow should be formally initiated;
furthermore, the practitioner of the vow must always provide gifts of food to those afflicted by hunger.
Indeed, it has been declared that the merit [of this field] is certainly superior to that of other heretical sites;
therefore, for one who gives food in this field, liberation stands within their grasp. 83.
O Brahmins, food must be given every day by one who desires merit;
however, everything becomes fruitless for him on this lunar day when the sacred field is turned away. 84.
The gift of food is declared to be superior to all other gifts;
therefore, O Brahmins, one who gives food in this most excellent field is indeed a giver of all gifts. (85)
There has never been, nor will there ever be, a gift superior to the gift of food;
indeed, the gift of food excels the gifts of elephants, horses, and chariots.
Those formerly skilled in knowledge have declared that the giver of food is the giver of everything;
therefore, the gift of food should always be made at the abode of Śiva.
O best of the twice-born, whatever man or woman performs the Cāturmāsya vow in this manner, O brahmins, they certainly obtain its fruit. (88)
Day by day, a human being obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice;
this is declared regarding the Rājasūya sacrifice for the month of Kārttika. ||89||
One attains the goals of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa without a doubt;
the wise Brāhmaṇa who knows the Vedas shall become so, and the king shall be victorious. ||90||
A Vaiśya shall become enriched with wealth, and a Śūdra shall attain a good rebirth; whatever sin has been committed in another field, it shall be destroyed in the abode of Śiva. ||91||
O best of men, sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, even those committed in other sacred fields, go to their destruction once one has entered this field. 92.
Sin committed in another field is destroyed at Svarṇakūṭa;
however, sin committed at Svarṇakūṭa certainly becomes as indelible as adamantine cement. ||93||
The sages said:
"O best of the twice-born, you have stated that a sin committed in this sacred field becomes as indelible as diamond-paste; by what means, then, can its destruction be brought about? (94)
Bharadvāja said:

O best of the twice-born, whatever man, with self-restraint, performs a circumambulation of the sacred field on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Māgha, [attains great merit]. ||95||
To the south, east, west, and likewise to the north of the Lord, there is a supreme field extending for one krośa belonging to Śiva, the Parameṣṭhin. ||96||
O twice-born ones, whoever performs a circumambulation of Meru, the destroyer of the sun, his committed sin is destroyed; of this there is no doubt. (97)
There, the wise man should remain silent and observe the vow of fasting;
indeed, in a single day, he should perform the circumambulation of that place in its entirety. ||98||
One should not remain even for a moment [in a state of distraction], nor should there be laughter or weeping; O Brahmins, if there is laughter or weeping, the circumambulation is indeed fruitless.
By circumambulating the sacred field once, the sins of ten million births are destroyed;
by a second time, those of a second [ten million]; and by a third time, those of three [ten million] births.
O best of the twice-born, for the destruction of sins committed at Ekāmra, there is no other path than the circumambulation of this sacred field. 101.
Sin committed at any other sacred site is destroyed at Svarṇakūṭa;
sin committed at Svarṇakūṭa is destroyed by performing a circumambulation.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Procedure for the Cāturmāsya Vow," in the dialogue between the sage Bharadvāja and [the Lord] within the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||18||
Now begins the nineteenth chapter.
The sages said:
O best of the twice-born, in this sacred field, the processions (yātrās) that are prescribed—
But, O Lord, tell us all of them in brief.
Bharadvāja said:
Seven pilgrimages are proclaimed in that Ekāmraka forest;
I shall describe them to you, O best of sages—listen! (2)
On the first eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, a pilgrimage is ordained there by Śambhu, the God of gods. ||3||
In former times, Śambhu gave this command to King Varuṇa: "On the first Aṣṭamī, I shall go to the vicinity of your Liṅga. (4)
From that time onwards, O Brahmins, there is a festival on the first eighth day (Prathamāṣṭamī);
bathing, recitation, and giving gifts performed there destroy all sins. ||5||
Now, O Brahmins, I shall describe by name the pilgrimage that destroys all sins, which was formerly commanded by Śambhu to the Sun-god.
Listen to my words, O King; out of affection for you, I shall speak.
On the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, there is a pilgrimage that destroys all sins.
On that lunar day, I shall come into the presence of your thousand-rayed Liṅga and bestow upon the worlds the highest fruit.
The gift of sesame seeds is said there to bestow great merit;
therein, the worship of Śrī Bhāskareśa is the characteristic mark of liberation. ||9||
Likewise, I shall further describe the proximity of the great-souled Kapila and that of the trident-bearing God of gods.
O sage, when the Kapila Liṅga is worshipped, a boon was granted by Kapardin; there, indeed, I accept worship with my whole being.
When there shall be a Sunday during the bright fortnight of the month of Phālguna, on that day I will perform a pilgrimage together with Umā, my auspicious consort.
I shall grant the supreme desired fruit to living beings, and especially to those who partake [of the offerings] in this sacred field of Kapila. (13)
Having applied oil and performed an immersion of the head and body in the Kapila lake,
one should duly perform the ritual bath there with this mantra.
Salutations to Kapila-tīrtha, which bestows the fruit of the Gaṅgā and the ocean;
O Tīrtha, destroy my sin as I immerse myself in your waters. (15)
Having recited this mantra, one should perform a bath there;
it will destroy sins such as the killing of a Brahmin—of this there is no doubt. (16)
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished right there.
Now I shall describe another pilgrimage, the one at Aśokā, which yields great fruit. (17)
O brahmins, in ancient times the Blessed Lord became pleased with Rādhava;
he, who is skilled in speech and possesses supreme vigor, spoke these sweet words.
O Rāma, Rāma, O mighty-armed descendant of Raghu, listen to my words; for the liberation of all beings, I shall describe a pilgrimage of great fruit. (19)
And when the eighth day of the bright fortnight arrives in the month of Caitra,
you shall be with Girijā in the presence of my Liṅga on the southern mountain.
Seeing me there stationed upon my chariot, one is liberated from sins such as the killing of a Brahmin; of this there is no doubt, nor even from birth as a Cāṇḍāla.
From that time forward, O Brahmins, she became known as Aśokāsyā because of her great fruit;
now I shall describe another pilgrimage, namely the one to Madanāntikā.
On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, one who worships Śiva with Madana shall certainly go to the world of Śiva, liberated from all sins. ||23||
However, a special [observance] must be performed in the presence of Śrītīrtheśvara;
now, O Lord, I shall describe another pilgrimage in the vicinity of Rāma.
That very linga known as Śrī Rāmeśvara, which was worshipped by Rāma, is the one approved by Rāma, the son of Jamadagni. ||25||
And on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, it is proclaimed that Hara formerly granted a boon to Rāma, the son of Jamadagni.
I shall go into your presence for the destruction of the life-breaths of living beings;
now I will speak of another [mantra] called the second, which yields great fruit. (27)
O Brahmins, on the second day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, especially so, a pilgrimage in the presence of Śrī Yameśvara bestows all desires. (28)
Thus, O observers of great vows, this seventh pilgrimage has been described;
O Brahmins, what more of the Purāṇa do you wish to hear? (29)
Kapila said:
Having heard these words spoken by Bharadvāja at that time,
they departed for the forest, their eyes filled with tears of joy.
On the first day, they all went to the city of Vārāṇasī;
having bathed in the waters of the Jāhnavī, they beheld the supreme liṅga.
Then those best of sages attained incomparable joy,
and once again they worshipped Maheśvara, the God of gods.
And on the very second day, the Brahmins reached the Gaṅgā;
there, the offering of funeral cakes and other rites were performed by the hand of Gādādharasvāmin.
Then, after many days, they reached Viraja-maṇḍalā;
having bathed in the waters of the Vaitaraṇī, they beheld him in a form of wrath.
Then they [worshipped] the goddess Virajā, the god Mukteśvara Hara, Akhaṇḍaleśvara, and Trilocana Maheśvara. ||35||
Then those best of the twice-born reached the river Brāhmī, which flows toward the eastern ocean and destroys all sins; there they performed their ablutions.
On the third day, O King, they went to the Ekāmraka forest;
having gone there, those best of sages beheld the hermitages.
O lord of the earth, having taken refuge at Siddhāśrama, they attained great joy;
thus it was, O best of kings, in the ancient and most excellent holy site of Puṣkara. (38)
And he related the conversation between the sages and the wise Bharadvāja concerning the excellent region of Utkala, for the sake of his satisfaction. (39)
And now, O protector of the earth, what else do you wish to hear regarding this supreme merit and the majesty of Utkala? ||40||
He whose hair stands on end while hearing this attains a meritorious state; so too does that best of men who recites this narrative called *Utkalākhyāna*. ||41||
O lord of the earth, those who hear this greatness of Utkala go to the supreme abode, which is difficult even for the gods and others to attain. 42.
Those best of men who perform this supreme merit shall obtain the fruit of the gift of a thousand cows. (43)
His intellect, established in the Dharma, shall never waver at any time. ||44||
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Attainment of Liberation by the Devas," in the dialogue between Bharadvāja and the Sage Kapila within the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||19||
Now begins the twentieth chapter.
Satyajit said:
"I have heard the ancient laws and the descriptions of the rivers."
Having heard of many sacred fords, my sin has gone to dissolution. ||1||
The illustrious Kapila said:
"I have previously described the fruitful sacred fields; now, O lord of the earth, listen as I speak of them. (2)
O King, that great river which was previously described as destroying many sins has a daughter known as Dakṣiṇāgamā, who flows toward the south.
That river was brought by the high-souled Bhṛgu through his ascetic power;
therefore, she is known as Bhārgavī, bestowing the fruit of a thousand cows.
Siddheśvarī is likewise [described] in brief; and in the account of the slaying of Siddheśvarī, Bhārgavī was brought by Bhṛgu, bestowing fruit equal to that of the Gaṅgā. ||5||
O protector of the earth, on its bank where there is a Śiva-liṅga, she is renowned as the bestower of liberation, especially when facing [the devotee]. ||6||
O best of kings, learn this meritorious bathing mantra, for without the bathing mantra, the bath becomes fruitless. (7)
O daughter of Bhṛgu, salutations to you, who bestow the fruit of a thousand cows;
may my sins go to dissolution upon immersion in your waters. (8)
Having spoken thus, one should bathe in that [river] and offer libations to the ancestors and the gods;
one attains the supreme abode together with twenty-one generations of one's lineage.
O King, her daughter was renowned as Puṣyabhadrā; she was famous for flowing toward the eastern ocean in the eastern direction. ||10||
O protector of the earth, bathing in that [river] during the month of Kārttika grants all desires;
likewise in Māgha and Āṣāḍha, and especially so in Phālguna. ||11||
The river which is Puṣyabhadrā is undoubtedly the Kṛṣṇā; it is for her pure water that the ancestors and deities long. ||12||
O best of kings, having entered another daughter of hers,
she became renowned as Dadhīnādā in the vicinity of the Ekāmravana forest.
And this [river] was brought by the sage Dadhīca, the ascetic; merely by bathing in its waters, a person shall go to the world of Soma. ||14||
O King, the Liṅga of Vyomakeśa is seen right there;
one should diligently perform a ritual bath at that spot on its bank. (15)
O best of men, the performer of the bath obtains a hundredfold, even a thousandfold, more fruit than from any other bath, as well as his desired object.
O protector of the earth, listen to me regarding the Eastern Guptasarasvatī,
by which the entire world of moving and non-moving beings, when consumed by the fire of time, was protected.
O Lord of the Earth, one yojana to the east of the Ekāmra forest,
there lies the river Sarasvatī, renowned by the name Prācī.
In the eastern direction, where there is the confluence of the ocean with Maheśa, there is a liṅga on every krośa along the bank; from that point flows the Prācī Sarasvatī. ||19||
O protector of the earth, having bathed in that [tirtha], a man shall go to the world of light,
completely liberated from all sins along with twenty-seven generations of his lineage.
O best of kings, the eastern Sarasvatī is the bestower of all merit, worthy of honor, and the direct giver of the abode of Vaikuṇṭha; it is not so in any other direction.
And at every *krośa* along its delightful bank, there are sacred emblems (*liṅga*s), everywhere easy to traverse and well-served by learned men. (22)
There, Hara is known as Vighneśvara, who dwells at the root of obstacles;
having seen and worshipped him, a person shall attain Śiva. ||23||
O protector of the earth, the Vighna tree on this earth is equal to the Kalpa-tree;
by circumambulating it, one is liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin. ||24||
There is the confluence of the three rivers (Triveṇī), which bestows great merit; O protector of the earth, bathing there during the month of Māgha is highly praised. ||25||
I shall specifically proclaim the great fruit of the new moon day (amāvāsyā): bathing, twilight prayers, austerity, and charity are declared to be inexhaustible on that occasion. (26)
Having performed his ablutions according to the prescribed rite at the Pāṇḍava Tīrtha in the east, he attains the destruction of his sins and shall go to the world of Śiva. ||27||
I shall describe the great Liṅga on its bank, namely Amareśvara;
by beholding Amareśa, a man shall not come to birth again. ||28||
On its bank is the god Maheśa, known by the name Kapileśvara; he is the deity who removes all sins, and his linga has been worshipped by me. (29)
Thus, there are many sacred marks on her auspicious bank;
O Lord of the Earth, who is able to describe all her virtues? (30)
I have related this in brief to you, as you asked out of your own interest.
Satyajit said:
"I have heard the entire greatness of Utkala."
And now, O best of sages, tell me of the yoga of knowledge.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the description of the majesty of Utkala within the glorious Kapila Purāṇa. ||20||
Now begins the twenty-first chapter.
Kapila said:
O lord of men, I shall declare the supreme secret of the yoga of knowledge.
Listen with a one-pointed mind, if faith arises within you. ||1||
O sinless one, this was heard by me in the past from Śambhu, the God of gods, in the dialogue with Nandikeśvara; listen to it once more now.
Salutations to you, O Lord of Pārvatī, O mine of compassion for devotees!
How may a living being be liberated from the cycle of existence and the bondage of karma? (3)
Mahādeva said: "To whatever living being who, having abandoned desire and anger, indeed worships me, I grant supreme liberation; there is no doubt in this. (4)
O son, when a person abandons desire and anger, then this [Self] residing within his heart attains manifestation. ||5||
Those men who, accompanied by sons and wives, take delight [in worldly things],
do not know the Supreme Light, the Lord Nārāyaṇa, who resides within the heart.
Those ignoble ones, the lowest of men, who sport with those deluded by pride—their residence in hell is certain; this is the truth, the great truth that has been proclaimed. (7)
O Nandikeśvara, you must abandon desire, anger, pride, delusion, violence, as well as malice, egoism, and greed. 8.
He who abandons mental and verbal resolve through action, indeed crosses the ocean of worldly existence by the chanting of Hari’s name alone. ||9||
Having placed the nectar of the Lord’s names in his mouth, that best of Vaiṣṇavas is thereafter free from all desires and mental constructs, even regarding the ocean.
Just as Hari is the Lord of the universe, so am I the Master of the worlds; there is no difference between us two, just as there is none between the wind and the sky. ||11||
Chant the name of Hari, the name of Hari, incessantly;
it bestows supreme liberation and union [with Him], of this there is no doubt. (12)
Place your trust in that Hari, the leader of the three worlds,
by whose illusory power even Brahmā is perpetually deluded.
O son, cultivate firm devotion toward me, Govinda, who am above the world and whose nature is the wind; thus you shall be released from your firm bondage.
I too am to be honored by you; I do not act, yet Śaṅkara acts, as does Nīlakaṇṭha, Śrīdhara, and Nīlavigraha. ||15||
Gaurīśa is the beloved of Gopikā; for those who meditate with one-pointed mind, there is no perceived difference whatsoever between Mādhava and Umādhava. 16.
The deluded create division, and they indeed suffer in the Raurava hell.
Kapila said:
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Śambhu became silent; then Nandin addressed Pārvatī’s Lord once more. 18.
Furthermore, I wish to hear about the marks of that high-souled Viṣṇu and of his devotees; O Compassionate One, tell me this. (19)
Śrī Mahādeva said: A body marked with the conch and the discus, adorned with a garland of tulasī,
and completely free from desire and anger— this indeed is the sign known as that of a Vaiṣṇava.
Among these, the loincloth is the best; sweet speech in the mouth, and a heart always full of bliss—these are indeed the marks of one known as a Vaiṣṇava. (21)
The loud chanting of Govinda's names accompanied by tears of joy and the renunciation of all attachments are indeed the marks of one designated as a Vaiṣṇava. 23.
That which is called "possessing all" is the state of awakened consciousness that brings happiness to all sentient beings; endowed with compassion and truth, it is indeed the mark known as Vaiṣṇava.
Free from the sense of "mine" and free from egoism, honoring the deities and Brahmins, and generating delight in the virtuous—this indeed is the mark of one known as a Vaiṣṇava. ||25||
Thus, he who possesses the marks of a Vaiṣṇava is indeed a Vaiṣṇava;
for others who are hypocritical and greedy, their outward signs are no cause [for being considered such]. ||26||
Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Śambhu entered the interior of the cave where Gaurī sports; there stands the doorkeeper Nandin, holding his staff.
Thus, this dialogue with Nandikeśvara—meritorious, secret, and bringing all peace—has been told to you by me, as it was spoken by Lord Śambhu. 28.
The Yoga of Knowledge should not be taught to one who is not a Vaiṣṇava, nor to those who revile the gods or Brahmins; it should not be taught to one whose mind is defiled by doubt. (29)
The person who reads this supreme secret, the yoga of knowledge, or even he who hears it with devotion, attains peace. ||30||
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Greatness of the Four Sacred Fields," within the narrative of the Utkala-kṣetra in the glorious Kapila Purāṇa.
This Kapila Purāṇa is now complete.
By means of this new work, may the world attain joy.
May Lord Viśvanātha, together with Bhavānī, be gracious;
it is my auspicious prayer that learned scholars may act in such a way that the propagation of the Purāṇas and Upapurāṇas may come to pass.
